review_outcome: Completed zero-write review. The current server composition cannot successfully confirm an organization installation because it does not inject administrator_authorizer. This verifies the review only; it does not accept the blocked Stage 1 node or establish release readiness.

findings.title: The production CLI omits administrator_authorizer, so POST /organization/provision/confirm always fails before confirmation work begins.
findings.evidence: Stage1ProvisioningRuntime permits an injected Callable[[AccountSession, str], TrustedFeishuAdministrator], but server_cli constructs it with only connection_factory and gateway. confirm_for_session checks for None before repository work and raises feishu_administrator_authorization_unavailable with HTTP 503.
findings.impact: No local or server launch through server_cli can complete the confirmation route, even when an authenticated owner, CSRF token, and idempotency key are valid.
findings.minimum_fix: Build and inject a server-only administrator authorizer in server_cli; do not bypass the None check or manufacture TrustedFeishuAdministrator from request data.

findings.title: Existing OAuth, identity-link, and installation-event state does not prove all required administrator authorization claims.
findings.evidence: The required object has tenant_key, open_id, scopes, expires_at, and is_tenant_administrator. Verified installation events establish installation/app/tenant_key only. Identity links persist an active or revoked tenant_key/open_id pair only. The inspected OAuth login path consumes tenant_key/open_id to create a platform session and does not carry administrator status, tenant:provision scope, or an authorization expiry into the provisioning path. A repository-wide producer search found TrustedFeishuAdministrator.from_server_adapter only in tests, not in production composition.
findings.impact: The existing state can be used as an identity and tenant consistency check, but cannot safely create the required TrustedFeishuAdministrator. Treating a VERIFIED string or a stable identity pair as an administrator grant would create a privilege escalation.
findings.minimum_fix: At confirmation time, use a server-held provider credential or a server-persisted, one-time, expiry-bounded administrator grant to verify the active identity pair, tenant administrator status, required scope, and expiry.

findings.title: credentialRef is accepted from the browser and becomes durable credential-selection state used by later provisioning.
findings.evidence: The HTTP forbidden-field set excludes credentialRef, then forwards body.get(credentialRef). The service only performs lexical normalization, records the value in the confirmation digest, and assigns it to the installation. start_for_session later loads the stored credential_ref into ResourceBindingContext for external resource work.
findings.impact: A request can select arbitrary durable credential-reference material without a server-side ownership, installation, tenant, freshness, or secret-store check. Depending on the downstream resolver, this can produce cross-tenant credential confusion or persist material that should never have entered from the browser.
findings.minimum_fix: Remove credentialRef from the HTTP request entirely. Resolve an opaque credential reference server-side from the verified installation and administrator grant, validate it against the selected installation and tenant, and pass a trusted typed grant or server-owned value into confirmation.

findings.title: Platform admin is implicitly converted to tenant support and may bypass the organization-workspace gate for start, status, and deprovision operations.
findings.evidence: The route admits a session whose global role is admin even outside organization_lark. actor_for_session then maps global admin to support without a tenant-scoped support assignment, current membership readback, or support-grant expiry. ProvisionOrchestrator only validates the trusted marker, not the role's provenance. Existing authorization coverage separately asserts that a platform admin cannot select or read another tenant, but it does not cover this support conversion or the Stage 1 control plane.
findings.impact: A global control-plane role is being treated as tenant-scoped operational authority. Confirmation still requires an owner record, but support can start or deprovision once the runtime derives the actor.
findings.minimum_fix: Make support an explicit tenant-scoped, auditable, expiry-bounded authorization source. If product policy does not authorize that role, remove the global-admin workspace bypass and map only an active tenant owner to the provision actor.

findings.title: The current runtime errors and HTTP envelope are outside the frozen Stage 1 OpenAPI error contract, and no composition or endpoint test catches it.
findings.evidence: The contract declares closed Stage 1 error codes, but feishu_administrator_authorization_unavailable and the admin_confirmation_* codes are not in the enumerated list. The route returns the generic {ok:false,error:{code,message}} envelope, while the declared Stage 1 response schema requires a different closed error shape. No test references Stage1ProvisioningRuntime, confirm_for_session, /organization/provision/confirm, or administrator_authorizer.
findings.impact: Clients cannot rely on the frozen control-plane interface for retry/reauthorization behavior, and an authorization failure may appear as an undocumented response.
findings.minimum_fix: Obtain interface-freeze approval to add a precise request/response and error mapping, or map only to approved generic closed codes without leaking provider details. Add HTTP contract tests before release.

tenant_key.evidence: A real TrustedInstallationEventAdapter can verify/decrypt an event and bind tenant_key to an installation; the service also detects cross-bound app or tenant identity.
tenant_key.limitations: The inspected server_cli composition does not construct an InstallationEventService or its adapter, and tenant_key alone is not administrator authorization.

open_id.evidence: IdentityLinkRecord stores tenant_key/open_id with active or revoked status, and the OAuth login handler receives a verified pair before platform login.
open_id.limitations: The identity-link result type accepts a status string and a stable pair but contains no administrator claim, scope, grant provenance, or authorization expiry. It must be independently rechecked against the active session and provider evidence.

administrator_status.evidence: TrustedFeishuAdministrator has is_tenant_administrator, but no production producer was found; the only direct factory uses are test fixtures.

required_scope.evidence: tenant:provision is a local constant and is checked by confirmation, but no OAuth, install-event, identity-link, or server-cli path supplies it.

expiry.evidence: Identity-link intents and OAuth scan attempts have their own expiries, but the inspected provisioning path has no persisted or live administrator-grant expiry.

implementation_recommendation.minimum_safe_closure: Introduce one server-only administrator authorization adapter and wire it into server_cli. It must resolve the current platform session's active tenant identity, verify a provider-backed or server-persisted administrator grant for the expected installation tenant, select the credential reference server-side, and return a trusted context. Browser input must contain no identity or credential-selector fields.

proposed_interface.name: Stage1AdministratorAuthorizer

return_shape.administrator: TrustedFeishuAdministrator created only after server-side verification of tenant_key, open_id, is_tenant_administrator, tenant:provision, and expires_at
return_shape.credential: trusted server-selected opaque credential reference bound to the same installation and tenant

required_checks: Resolve one active server-side identity link for session.user_id and session.tenant_id; reject missing, ambiguous, revoked, or tenant/open_id mismatch.
Verify or read a fresh administrator grant using server-held provider credentials; never trust browser fields, a VERIFIED status string, or a stable identity pair as a grant.
Require the expected tenant_key, is_tenant_administrator true, tenant:provision present, and expires_at later than the server clock.
Resolve credential_ref from the verified installation/grant on the server and check installation and tenant ownership before it reaches ResourceBindingContext.
Audit the grant identity, installation, decision, and non-secret reference identifier; do not log OAuth tokens, raw credentials, ciphertext, or browser-supplied values.

error_handling: Return a fail-closed 403 for missing/revoked/ambiguous identity, tenant or open_id mismatch, non-administrator, missing scope, and expired grant.
Return a sanitized 503 for unavailable provider verification, unavailable credential store, or unconfigured server credential; do not fall back to platform admin or cached identity alone.
Reject a confirm body containing credentialRef or any identity/role/installation field with 403. The normal body should be empty until an approved request schema says otherwise.
Map all outcomes to approved frozen OpenAPI error codes and response schema before changing the public endpoint.
implementation_recommendation.not_authorized_by_this_review: No source, migration, credential configuration, deployment, or SSOT acceptance is authorized by this review.

required_files.change: New server-only adapter that combines active server identity evidence, provider/admin-grant verification, expiry checks, and installation-owned credential selection.

Add a marked trusted credential/grant boundary so AdministratorConfirmationService cannot receive a browser-originated raw credential_ref string. Preserve the existing administrator, scope, expiry, and tenant checks.
Consume AuthorizedProvisioningContext from the authorizer, remove the credential_ref argument from confirm_for_session, and fail closed when the authorizer cannot supply a verified context.

Construct the authorizer from explicit server configuration and account/provider repositories, fail startup or return a deterministic unavailable state when the required credential configuration is absent, and inject it into Stage1ProvisioningRuntime.
Reject credentialRef as a browser field, retain CSRF and idempotency requirements, and translate the authorizer's sanitized errors into the approved contract response.
Only after interface-freeze approval: define the confirm request as server-derived/no credential selector and add or approve the exact closed error mapping and response envelope.

required_tests.coverage: Active identity plus matching tenant/open_id/admin/scope/future expiry succeeds; missing, revoked, ambiguous, cross-tenant, non-admin, missing-scope, expired, and unavailable-provider paths fail closed without secret leakage.
Replace raw credential_ref fixture input with a trusted server grant and assert direct untrusted credential values are rejected. Keep atomic and idempotent confirmation coverage.
Default missing authorizer returns 503; injected authorizer is called with the session and server-derived expected tenant_key; only its server-selected credential reaches confirmation.

Exercise /openclaw/media/api/organization/provision/confirm with session, CSRF, and idempotency. Verify empty-body success with a fake trusted authorizer; reject tenant/openId/role/installationId/credentialRef; assert approved 403 and 503 contracts.
Verify server_cli supplies the authorizer in HTTP composition and fails deterministically when required server configuration is absent.
Validate the frozen request and error schema against the actual confirm route, including no browser credential selector.

decisions_needed.why: Choose the supported Feishu API/grant that proves tenant administrator status and determine whether tenant:provision is a provider scope or an application-local, server-signed policy scope. This cannot be inferred from the current OAuth login or install-event data.

Decide whether provisioning uses an app-owned server credential selected solely from installation state or a per-tenant credential stored in an approved server-side vault. The browser must never select the reference.
Decide whether global platform admins may act as tenant-scoped support. If yes, define an explicit tenant assignment, audit, and expiry; if no, remove the implicit mapping and workspace bypass.
Approve exact public request and error semantics or require mapping to existing closed generic codes. This review must not alter the frozen contract.

commands.result: review evidence: production contains the injectable slot only; direct trusted-administrator factory uses were test fixtures.

residual_risks: Passing focused tests prove pure service behavior and selected authorization semantics, not CLI composition, HTTP confirm behavior, provider credential availability, or a real Feishu administrator readback.
No live provider, local deployment, database migration, external credential store, or production system was touched by this zero-write review.
The Stage 1 SSOT node remains formally blocked until an approved credential and support policy is implemented and independently verified against the frozen acceptance path.
The candidate backend directory is not itself a Git worktree, so this review did not use Git diff as evidence; no candidate source, test, migration, manifest, contract, or SSOT file was edited.
